questions.question: Describe the graph of y = x² fully — its shape, turning point, axis of symmetry, domain and range — and explain why the left half mirrors the right half.
questions.expected_answer: The graph of y = x² is a smooth curve lying entirely on or above the x-axis. Its lowest point, the turning point, is at the origin (0; 0), and because the curve opens upward this turning point is a minimum. The axis of symmetry is the vertical line x = 0, which is the y-axis. The domain is all real values of x, because any real number can be squared. The range is y ≥ 0, because a square is never negative — and the range must be written in terms of y, not x. The two halves mirror each other because squaring destroys the sign: x = −3 and x = 3 both give y = 9, x = −2 and x = 2 both give 4, and so on. The curve flattens and turns at the bottom rather than coming to a sharp point, and it rises ever more steeply as x moves away from zero.

questions.question: Explain the separate effects of a and q in y = ax² + q, including what each does to the turning point, the range and the number of x-intercepts.
questions.expected_answer: The sign of a decides direction: a positive a opens the parabola upward with a minimum turning point, a negative a opens it downward with a maximum. The size of a decides width: a value greater than 1 in size stretches the graph vertically and makes it narrower, while a value between 0 and 1 squashes it and makes it wider. With q = 0, changing a never moves the turning point off the origin. The parameter q shifts the whole graph vertically by q units and changes nothing else, so the turning point moves to (0; q), the y-intercept equals q, and the axis of symmetry stays x = 0. The range becomes y ≥ q when a is positive and y ≤ q when a is negative. For x-intercepts: when a and q have the same sign there are none, because solving gives x² equal to a negative number; when they have opposite signs there are two; and when q = 0 the curve touches the x-axis once, at the origin.

questions.question: Sketch y = 2x² − 8 in words, listing every feature a marker expects, then find the equation of a parabola y = ax² + q with turning point (0; −3) passing through (2; 5).
questions.expected_answer: For y = 2x² − 8: a = 2 is positive, so the parabola opens upward with a minimum. q = −8, so the turning point is (0; −8) and the y-intercept is (0; −8). The axis of symmetry is x = 0. For the x-intercepts, set y = 0: 2x² = 8, so x² = 4 and x = 2 or x = −2, giving (2; 0) and (−2; 0). The domain is all real x and the range is y ≥ −8. A useful extra point is (3; 10), since 2(9) − 8 = 10, with (−3; 10) by symmetry. The sketch is a smooth upward-opening curve with its lowest point on the y-axis at −8, cutting the x-axis at −2 and 2 and climbing steeply on both sides. For the second part: the turning point gives q = −3, so y = ax² − 3. Substituting (2; 5): 5 = a(2)² − 3, so 4a = 8 and a = 2. The equation is y = 2x² − 3.
